changed.title: The 8 by 8 graph with mask 11871860300395540620 is represented on the one-a-side promise by an AND/OR circuit of fan-in two with at most 24 gates
changed.statement: PEqualNP.Represents.RepSizeAtMost (fun u v : Fin 8 => (11871860300395540620 : ℕ).testBit (8 * u.val + v.val)) 24
changed.unlocks: the least cost of one dense 8 by 8 graph with no equal lines, approached from above
changed.sketch: We hold no circuit of this size; this is a search. Our circuit is the row star with shared ORs; pairs of columns that occur together in several rows may save gates.

changed.title: One fan-in-two circuit reads a table at many input addresses with shared gates
changed.statement:
∀ (a b q : ℕ),
  let words := 2 ^ a
  let I := words * b + q * a
  ∃ (C : PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.Circuit)
    (outBit : Fin q → Fin b → Fin (I + C.size)),
    PEqualNP.MetaComplexity.FanInTwo C ∧
    PEqualNP.MetaComplexity.NestedCover.ReadsBack I C ∧ C.output < I + C.size ∧
    C.size ≤ 128 * (words + q) * (a + b + Nat.log2 (q + 1) + 3) ^ 3 ∧
    ∀ (table : Fin words → Fin b → Bool) (address : Fin q → Fin words),
      let x := (List.ofFn (fun j : Fin words => List.ofFn (table j))).flatten ++
        (List.ofFn (fun j : Fin q =>
          List.ofFn (fun i : Fin a => (address j).val.testBit i.val))).flatten
      ∀ (j : Fin q) (i : Fin b),
        (C.wires x).getD (outBit j i).val false = table (address j) i
changed.unlocks: supplies shared table lookups for a bank of ranked cyclic words
changed.context: On paper. Pad table records and query records to a power of two. Sort them with a bitonic network on dummy flag, address and tag, tables before requests. Keep each comparator's swap bit. Scan the sorted records, carrying the latest table word. Every real query now has its answer. Run the swaps backwards on those answers to restore query order, even at repeated addresses. Charge comparison, swaps in both directions, the scan and the shared constants.

Keep each comparator's swap bit. Scan the sorted records, carrying the latest table word. Every real query now has its answer. Run the swaps backwards on those answers to restore query order, even at repeated addresses. Charge comparison, swaps in both directions, the scan and the shared constants.

changed.title: A balanced product gives a monotone depth bound for deciding arbitrary cyclic window tables
changed.statement:
∀ (n w : ℕ) (hn : 0 < n),
  let I := n * 2 ^ (w + 1)
  ∃ C : PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.Circuit,
    PEqualNP.MetaComplexity.Monotone2 C ∧
    PEqualNP.MetaComplexity.NestedCover.ReadsBack I C ∧ C.output < I + C.size ∧
    C.size ≤ 6 * n * 8 ^ w + 3 ∧
    C.depth I ≤ 1 + (Nat.log2 n + 1) * (w + 1) + w ∧
    ∀ table : Fin n → (Fin (w + 1) → Bool) → Bool,
      let x := (List.ofFn (fun i : Fin n => List.ofFn (fun p : Fin (2 ^ (w + 1)) =>
        table i (fun j => p.val.testBit j.val)))).flatten
      C.eval x = true ↔ ∃ word : Fin n → Bool, ∀ i : Fin n,
        table i (fun j => word ⟨(i.val + j.val) % n, Nat.mod_lt _ hn⟩) = true
changed.unlocks: gives a parallel table decision circuit of bounded depth and size at each width
changed.context: At each position form the Boolean transition matrix on w-bit windows, using either appended bit. With w=0 OR both input bits in the single cell. Pad the list with identity matrices to a power of two and multiply in a balanced tree. Each product uses one AND layer and w binary OR layers per entry. OR its diagonal to test for a permitted path returning to its initial window. The closure gives an indexed cyclic word even when w exceeds n. Count gates and longest paths in the same list. Gate-price companions cannot exist for this constructive ceiling.

Gate-price companions cannot exist for this constructive ceiling.

changed.title: At most 2+e private rows have distinct profiles outside a narrow column set in an AND/OR region with e at most one entry wire
changed.statement:
∀ (n m d : ℕ) (G : Fin n → Fin m → Bool) (C : PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.Circuit)
    (R : Finset (Fin n)) (B : Finset (Fin m)) (region entry : Finset ℕ) (top : ℕ),
  let raw := n + m
  let sources := R.image (fun sourceRow => sourceRow.val) ∪ B.image (fun sourceCol => n + sourceCol.val)
  let inside := fun (w : ℕ) => raw ≤ w ∧ w - raw ∈ region
  let gate := PEqualNP.MetaComplexity.NestedCover.gateAt C
  (∀ firstRow secondRow : Fin n, firstRow ≠ secondRow → d ≤ (Finset.univ.filter (fun col => G firstRow col ≠ G secondRow col)).card) →
  (∀ firstCol secondCol : Fin m, firstCol ≠ secondCol → d ≤ (Finset.univ.filter (fun row => G row firstCol ≠ G row secondCol)).card) →
  PEqualNP.MetaComplexity.NestedCover.ReadsBack raw C →
  PEqualNP.Represents.Represents G C → region ⊆ Finset.range C.size → top ∈ region →
  entry.card ≤ 1 → (∀ w ∈ entry, w < raw + top ∧ w ∉ sources ∧ ¬ inside w) →
  (∀ k ∈ region,
    ((gate k).op = PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.GateOp.and ∨
     (gate k).op = PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.GateOp.or) ∧
    ∀ w ∈ (gate k).inputs, w ∈ sources ∨ inside w ∨ w ∈ entry) →
  (∀ k < C.size, k ∉ region → ∀ w ∈ (gate k).inputs,
    w ∉ sources ∧ (inside w → w = raw + top)) →
  C.output ∉ sources → (inside C.output → C.output = raw + top) →
  (B.card < d → R.card ≤ 2 + entry.card) ∧ (R.card < d → B.card ≤ 2 + entry.card)
changed.unlocks: bounds the number of private rows or columns whose profiles differ outside a small opposite set
changed.context: Fix an active outside column and vary the active private row. Until the top, outside gates cannot read a private signal, so the entry value depends only on the column. In the region each row induces a monotone unary truth table on that bit, either zero, identity or one. Without an entry there are two constant tables. Equal tables give identical outputs on every outside column, since only the top leaves the region. Fewer than d private columns cannot hide d disagreements. Count the types and exchange sides. Gate-price companions cannot exist for a bound on private inputs.

Gate-price companions cannot exist for a bound on private inputs.

changed.title: One-a-side promise: the 4 by 5 bipartite graph with mask 103928 has a fan-in-two AND/OR circuit of at most 11 gates
changed.statement: PEqualNP.Represents.RepSizeAtMost (fun (u : Fin 4) (v : Fin 5) => (103928 : ℕ).testBit (5 * u.val + v.val)) 11
changed.unlocks: the AND/OR cost of 4 by 5 graphs off the square, where the checked twin merge sends square graphs, for the silent-line work
changed.sketch: A search unit. We hold a circuit of 12 AND/OR gates (three plain forms, full lines taken out and equal gates merged); at this size those forms are weak; we hold none of 11; this is a search. Our count of unread rows and columns gives a floor of 8 (on paper), a gap of 4. Answer with a gate list (AND or OR, each reading at most two wires; wires 0 to 3 left, 4 to 8 right, gate j writes wire 9 + j, each gate reading only earlier wires) and its output wire, judged on all 20 inputs with one vertex on each side.

changed.title: The two-lit function of the graph H on 6 points with mask 17051 on shared wires has an AND/OR/NOT circuit of fan-in two with at most 9 gates
changed.statement: ∃ C : PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.Circuit, PEqualNP.MetaComplexity.FanInTwo C ∧ C.size ≤ 9 ∧ ∀ i j : Fin 6, C.eval (List.ofFn fun k : Fin 6 => decide (k = i ∨ k = j)) = (17051 : ℕ).testBit (6 * min i.val j.val + max i.val j.val)
changed.unlocks: the exact size of the two-lit-points function of this graph on six shared wires; the family shows where a NOT gate pays with no equal lines
changed.sketch: We hold a circuit of 10 gates, a weak hand form (best over a few point orders and the complement plus a NOT, equal gates merged): NOT(0), AND(4,6), OR(0,1), NOT(8), AND(3,9), AND(2,8), OR(5,7), OR(10,12), OR(11,13), NOT(14) (inputs 0-5 are the points, gate k is wire 6 + k, output last). We hold no circuit of 9 gates; this is a search. No complete search of ours has run at six points.

changed.title: An AND/OR/NOT circuit of fan-in at most two with at most 58 gates computes the edge function of the listed graph on 25 vertices with 48 edges
changed.unlocks: one search on a named graph: is there a circuit one gate smaller than the best we know for its edge function; a found circuit is a bound from above, a proof of none a bound from below
changed.context: SKETCH: truth not known to us; the opposite row is offered beside it. Proved by exhibiting ONE circuit with at most the stated number of gates of fan-in at most two that computes the edge function (true exactly when both ends of some edge are true) on every input; checked by evaluation. The best circuit known to us has one gate more (computed, not checked). Size: minutes if such a circuit exists. No sorry, no new axiom. Own namespace for every declaration.
